_description: Historical block bootstrap combined with the widow's-penalty survivor model where the SPOUSE outlives self (self 65→80, spouse 60→92). The projection horizon is the survivor's 33 years, not self's 16 — this scenario crashes (or silently reads cross-run returns) if any return generator sizes itself with the self-only horizon.
_rationale: Pure accumulation: $500k Roth, no spending, no income. Probability=100 because zero spending cannot deplete the balance. The load-bearing assertions are structural: the runner's length check pins the horizon to 33 years (spouse 92 − 60 + 1), and the run completing at all proves the bootstrap indexMap covers the survivor years (regression for the self-only-horizon indexMap overrun: HISTORICAL_RETURNS[undefined] → TypeError on the final run's survivor years). Median final balance uses the same broad 60/40 real-CAGR band as the other bootstrap tests, widened for the 33-year horizon.
name: Widow bootstrap survivor horizon
